title: Small but Powerful AI Models - Compact Knowledge Base
description: Research summary of efficient, small-parameter AI models that pack surprising capability

models.name: Phi-3.5 Mini
models.performance: Matches GPT-3.5 level on many tasks
models.efficiency: 95% smaller than larger models, 2-3x faster inference
models.notes: Best overall value. Can run on consumer hardware. Phi-3.5 Medium (7B) also available.

models.name: Mistral 7B
models.efficiency: Competitive with larger models, uses ~14GB VRAM
models.notes: Industry standard for 7B class. Mistral-Nemo (12B) = better version.

models.name: Llama 3.2 1B & 3B
models.performance: Matches Phi-3 level, better instruction following
models.notes: Best for resource-constrained environments. 3B better quality, still tiny.

models.name: Qwen 2.5 0.5B / 1.5B
models.performance: Exceeds Mistral 7B on many benchmarks despite tiny size
models.notes: Hidden gem. Qwen2.5-7B also available. Incredible quality-per-param.

models.name: Gemma 2B & 7B
models.notes: Google's answer to Phi. 2B version is competitive sweet spot.

models.name: TinyLlama 1.1B
models.notes: Great for research and education. Not production-ready for enterprise.

models.name: OLMo 1B & 7B
models.performance: Open weights, fully open training process
models.notes: For researchers & academics. Values transparency over commercial performance.

models.name: MPT-3B
models.notes: Good for commercial use. Instruction variant optimized for chat.

comparison_summary.best_overall: Phi-3.5 Mini (3.8B) - Balance of capability, speed, efficiency
comparison_summary.best_edge_device: Llama 3.2 1B - Runs on phones, reasonable capability
comparison_summary.best_for_coding: Phi-3.5 or Qwen 2.5 - Both excel at code generation

key_insights: Efficiency scaling: Parameters no longer determine capability. 3.8B models now compete with 13B+.
Quantization: 4-bit or 8-bit quantization reduces VRAM by 75% with minimal loss.
Local deployment: Most models here can run on consumer hardware with optimizations.
Emerging leaders: Qwen and Phi leading the 'capability-per-parameter' race.
Open vs proprietary: Open models now rival proprietary on many benchmarks.
Training cost: Training tiny models is accessible to researchers and startups.
Use-case driven: Pick by task (coding, chat, reasoning) not just parameters.

recommended: Primary: Qwen 2.5 1.5B (if GPU) or Phi-3.5 Mini (best all-rounder)
Secondary: Llama 3.2 3B (if CPU-only) or Mistral 7B (if more power)
recommendations_for_ram.integration: Can replace current local endpoint with any of these models
recommendations_for_ram.advantages: Better reasoning, code understanding, multilingual support
